## The desk question {.unnumbered}

A client buys a bond yielding 5%. **Will the client actually earn 5% over the
next two years?** Build a horizon-value report that separates coupon income,
reinvestment income, and the change in the bond's full price. Then explain
which assumptions make a quoted yield an attainable compound return.

## Purpose and assumptions {.unnumbered}

Use an illustrative five-year, 6% coupon bond with face value $100. Coupons are
semiannual. Buy immediately after a coupon at a 5% nominal annual YTM and sell
immediately after the year-2 coupon. All cash flows are contractual; ignore
default, calls, taxes, fees, and bid–ask spreads. Accrued interest is zero at both
endpoints. Exit YTM and coupon reinvestment rates are independent scenario inputs,
quoted as nominal annual rates compounded semiannually. No inputs are live quotes.

Read alongside [Lecture 2](../lecture_notes/lec2.qmd). Dollar results below are
per $100 face unless explicitly scaled to the client position.

```{python}

#| include: false

# Keep every field, but split wide tables into readable panels for HTML and PDF.
def readable_table(frame):
    """Format a teaching table without changing its underlying numerical values.

    Parameters
    ----------
    frame : pandas.DataFrame
        Display data. attrs["whole_table"] requests a single reconciliation
        table; attrs["decimals"] chooses the number of displayed decimals.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        HTML markup suitable for both Quarto HTML and PDF conversion.

    Notes
    -----
    Wide, short tables are transposed. Other wide tables are split into panels.
    Formatting applies only at display time, preserving full-precision results.
    """
    whole_table = frame.attrs.get("whole_table", False)
    decimals = frame.attrs.get("decimals", 4)
    frame = frame.copy()
    if not whole_table and len(frame.columns) and frame.iloc[:, 0].dtype == object:
        frame = frame.set_index(frame.columns[0])
    if not whole_table and len(frame.columns) > 6 and len(frame) <= 4:
        frame = frame.T
    panels = []
    panel_width = len(frame.columns) if whole_table else 3
    for start in range(0, len(frame.columns), panel_width):
        part = frame.iloc[:, start:start+panel_width]
        markup = part.to_html(border=0, na_rep="", float_format=lambda v: f"{v:,.{decimals}f}")
        widths = [40] + [60 / max(1, len(part.columns))] * len(part.columns)
        cols = "<colgroup>" + "".join(f'<col style="width:{w}%">' for w in widths) + "</colgroup>"
        end = markup.index(">") + 1
        panels.append(markup[:end] + cols + markup[end:])
    return "\n".join(panels)

get_ipython().display_formatter.formatters["text/html"].for_type(pd.DataFrame, readable_table)

def demo_explorer(x, series, x_label, y_label, initial=0):
    """Build an accessible HTML explorer from precomputed price-change series.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : array-like
        Strictly increasing finite scenario grid, in the units of x_label.
    series : dict[str, array-like]
        Named outputs, with one finite value for every x entry.
    x_label, y_label : str
        Axis labels including units.
    initial : int, default 0
        Zero-based row selected initially and by the Reset button.

    Returns
    -------
    IPython.display.HTML
        Self-contained chart, slider, reset control, and six-decimal table.

    Notes
    -----
    The browser selects stored Python results without interpolating prices.
    Use one instance per page because this helper uses fixed control IDs.
    """
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
    values = {name: np.asarray(y, dtype=float).tolist() for name, y in series.items()}
    assert len(x) > 1 and np.isfinite(x).all() and np.all(np.diff(x) > 0)
    assert 0 <= initial < len(x)
    assert all(len(y) == len(x) and np.isfinite(y).all() for y in values.values())
    payload = json.dumps({"x": x.tolist(), "series": values,
                          "xLabel": x_label, "yLabel": y_label,
                          "initial": int(initial)}, allow_nan=False).replace("<", "\\u003c")
    markup = """
<div class="demo-lab" style="border-left:4px solid #936724;padding:1rem;margin:1rem 0">
  <label for="demo-control"><strong>__XLABEL__</strong></label>

  <button id="demo-reset" type="button">Reset</button>
  <p id="demo-selection" aria-live="polite"></p>
  <svg id="demo-plot" viewBox="0 0 760 350" role="img"
       aria-label="__YLABEL__ as __XLABEL__ changes" style="width:100%;height:auto"></svg>
  <div style="overflow-x:auto"><table><thead><tr><th>Model output</th><th>__YLABEL__</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody id="demo-values"></tbody></table></div>
  <small>The control selects computed scenario points, not live market observations.</small>
</div>
<script>
(() => {
const d = __DATA__, slider = document.getElementById('demo-control');
const svg = document.getElementById('demo-plot'), ns = 'http://www.w3.org/2000/svg';
const colors = ['#214b3e','#936724','#486d8c','#865c76'];
const dash = ['', '8 4', '3 3', '10 3 2 3'];
const all = Object.values(d.series).flat(), lo = Math.min(...all), hi = Math.max(...all);
const pad = Math.max((hi-lo)*.12, .01), ymin = lo-pad, ymax = hi+pad;
let width=760;
const X = v => 70 + (width-100)*(v-d.x[0])/(d.x[d.x.length-1]-d.x[0]);
const Y = v => 275 - 240*(v-ymin)/(ymax-ymin);
/** Append an SVG element with attributes and optional accessible text. */
const add = (name, attrs, content='') => {

  if(content) e.textContent=content; svg.appendChild(e); return e;
};
// Axis ticks stay compact; the result table preserves small differences.
const fmt = v => v.toLocaleString('en-US',{maximumFractionDigits:3});
const precise = v => (v === 0 ? 0 : v).toLocaleString('en-US',{minimumFractionDigits:6,maximumFractionDigits:6});
/** Draw the selected scenario, marker, and accessible table values. */

  svg.setAttribute('viewBox','0 0 '+width+' 350');
  add('rect',{x:0,y:0,width:width,height:350,fill:'#ffffff'});
  for(let j=0;j<5;j++){

    add('line',{x1:70,y1:y,x2:width-30,y2:y,stroke:'#e0e3df'});
    add('text',{x:62,y:y+4,'text-anchor':'end',fill:'#333','font-size':12},fmt(v));

  for(let j=0;j<3;j++){

    add('text',{x:X(v),y:299,'text-anchor':'middle',fill:'#333','font-size':12},fmt(v));

  const tbody=document.getElementById('demo-values'); tbody.replaceChildren();
  Object.entries(d.series).forEach(([name,y],j)=>{

    add('circle',{cx:X(d.x[i]),cy:Y(y[i]),r:5,fill:colors[j%4],stroke:'white'});

    return HTML(markup.replace("__DATA__", payload)
                .replace("__XLABEL__", html.escape(x_label))
```

## Price the promised cash flows

With $n=10$ half-year periods and $C=100(0.06)/2=3$,

$$
P_0=\sum_{k=1}^{10}\frac{3}{(1+0.05/2)^k}
       +\frac{100}{(1+0.05/2)^{10}}.
$$

```{python}
#| label: returns-setup
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from IPython.display import Markdown, display

plt.rcParams.update({"figure.figsize": (8, 4.2), "font.size": 11,
    "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False,
    "axes.grid": True, "grid.alpha": .2})

def bond_price(coupon_rate, periods, annual_yield, face=100.):
    """Ex-coupon full price on a semiannual coupon date; rates are decimals.

    `periods` is the number of remaining half years. A zero-period bond has
    just matured and returns principal; coupon accounting is handled separately.
    Yield can be scalar or an array. Payment dates occupy the final axis.
    """
    y = np.asarray(annual_yield, dtype=float)
    if not np.all(np.isfinite(y)) or np.any(y <= -2):
        raise ValueError("Semiannual yields must be finite and greater than -200%.")
    if int(periods) != periods or periods < 0 or not 0 <= coupon_rate < 1 or face <= 0:
        raise ValueError("Use nonnegative integer periods, a valid coupon, and positive face.")
    if periods == 0:
        return np.full_like(y, face, dtype=float)
    k = np.arange(1, periods + 1)
    cf = np.full(periods, face*coupon_rate/2)
    cf[-1] += face
    return np.sum(cf*np.exp(-np.log1p(y[...,None]/2)*k), axis=-1)

def show_table(frame, decimals=4):
    """Keep short reports together in PDF and retain clear column labels."""
    if frame.shape[1] > 4:
        frame = frame.set_index(frame.columns[0]).T.reset_index().rename(columns={"index":"Measure"})
    reserve = "```{=latex}\n\\ReserveTableSpace{" + str(len(frame)+4) + "\\baselineskip}\n```\n\n"
    def cell(value):
        if isinstance(value, (int, float, np.number)):
            return f"{value:.{decimals}f}"
        return str(value).replace("|", "\\|")
    rows = ["| " + " | ".join(map(str, frame.columns)) + " |",
            "| " + " | ".join(["---"]*len(frame.columns)) + " |"]
    rows += ["| " + " | ".join(cell(v) for v in row) + " |"
             for row in frame.itertuples(index=False, name=None)]
    display(Markdown(reserve+"\n".join(rows)))

coupon_rate, maturity_periods, purchase_yield = .06, 10, .05
purchase_price = float(bond_price(coupon_rate, maturity_periods, purchase_yield))
periods = np.arange(1, 11)
cf = np.full(10, 3.); cf[-1] += 100
payments = pd.DataFrame({"Year": periods/2, "Payment": cf,
    "Discount factor": (1+purchase_yield/2)**(-periods),
    "Present value": cf/(1+purchase_yield/2)**periods})
show_table(payments,5)
display(Markdown(f"**Purchase full price: {purchase_price:.6f}.** The 6% coupon exceeds the 5% YTM, so the bond trades above par."))
```

## Distinguish quoted yields from realized returns

Current yield is annual coupon divided by today's price. It ignores both
reinvestment and the gain or loss when the bond is sold or redeemed. YTM is the
internal rate of return of promised payments at the purchase price. It is not a
forecast of a short-horizon sale price.

```{python}
#| label: return-quote-comparison
display(pd.DataFrame({"Measure": ["Coupon rate", "Current yield", "Nominal annual YTM", "Effective annual YTM"],
    "Percent": [6., 100*6/purchase_price, 5., 100*((1+.05/2)**2-1)]}).round(4))
```

A 5% semiannual-compounding YTM corresponds to an effective annual rate of
$(1.025)^2-1=5.0625\%$. Realizing that compound rate requires the relevant
reinvestment and terminal-value assumptions, as the next calculation shows.

## Build terminal wealth without double counting coupons

At $H=2$ years, four coupons have been received. The sale price is ex-coupon,
with six half-year payments remaining. If $j$ is the annual reinvestment rate,

$$
FV_C=3\left[(1+j/2)^3+(1+j/2)^2+(1+j/2)+1\right],
$$

$$
W_H=P_H+FV_C,\qquad
HPR=\frac{W_H-P_0}{P_0},\qquad
R_{\mathrm{annual}}=\left(\frac{W_H}{P_0}\right)^{1/H}-1.
$$

The coupon paid at year 2 enters $FV_C$ once and earns no reinvestment interest.
The sale price excludes that coupon. This is a terminal-wealth return that
assumes all coupon cash remains invested until the horizon.

```{python}
#| label: horizon-return-engine
def horizon_report(exit_yield, reinvest_rate, horizon_periods=4):
    """Return a scenario table of terminal wealth and realized return.

    Rates are decimal nominal annual rates; horizon is an integer number of
    half years in [1, 10]. Scalars and arrays broadcast to a common shape.
    Coupons are reinvested at a constant scenario rate, without withdrawals.
    """
    if int(horizon_periods) != horizon_periods or not 1 <= horizon_periods <= maturity_periods:
        raise ValueError("Horizon must be a coupon date through maturity.")
    ey, ri = np.broadcast_arrays(np.atleast_1d(exit_yield), np.atleast_1d(reinvest_rate))
    if not np.all(np.isfinite(ri)) or np.any(ri <= -2):
        raise ValueError("Reinvestment rates must be finite and greater than -200%.")
    coupon_cash = 3*horizon_periods
    powers = np.arange(horizon_periods-1, -1, -1)
    coupon_fv = 3*np.exp(np.log1p(ri[...,None]/2)*powers).sum(axis=-1)
    sale = bond_price(coupon_rate, maturity_periods-horizon_periods, ey)
    wealth = sale+coupon_fv
    return pd.DataFrame({"Exit YTM (%)": 100*ey.ravel(), "Reinvest (%)": 100*ri.ravel(),
        "Sale / principal": sale.ravel(), "Coupon cash": np.full(ey.size,coupon_cash),
        "Reinvestment income": (coupon_fv-coupon_cash).ravel(),
        "Price change": (sale-purchase_price).ravel(), "Terminal wealth": wealth.ravel(),
        "HPR (%)": 100*(wealth/purchase_price-1).ravel(),
        "Annual return (%)": 100*np.expm1(np.log(wealth/purchase_price)/(horizon_periods/2)).ravel()})

base = horizon_report(.05,.05)
show_table(base,5)
```

The unchanged-yield case includes a price decline toward par. Coupon income
more than offsets that decline. A premium bond's coupon rate therefore overstates
its return even when market yields do not change.

## Separate price risk from reinvestment risk

Hold reinvestment at 3% while varying exit yields. Then hold the exit yield at 5%
while varying reinvestment. This separation avoids assuming that sale yields and
all past reinvestment rates move together.

```{python}
#| label: returns-scenarios
scenarios = horizon_report([.03,.05,.10], .03)
show_table(scenarios,4)
show_table(horizon_report(.05,[.01,.03,.05]),4)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1,2,figsize=(9,4))
x = np.arange(3)
axes[0].bar(x, scenarios["Coupon cash"],label="Coupon cash",color="#214b3e")
axes[0].bar(x, scenarios["Reinvestment income"],bottom=scenarios["Coupon cash"],label="Reinvestment",color="#936724")
axes[0].bar(x, scenarios["Price change"],label="Price change",color="#486d8c",alpha=.8)
axes[0].set(xticks=x,xticklabels=["3%","5%","10%"] ,xlabel="Exit YTM",ylabel="Return component per $100 face")
axes[0].axhline(0,color="grey",lw=1);axes[0].legend(fontsize=8)
yields=np.linspace(.01,.10,91)
for j in [.01,.03,.05]:
    result=horizon_report(yields,j)
    axes[1].plot(100*yields,result["Annual return (%)"],label=f"Reinvest {100*j:.0f}%")
axes[1].set(xlabel="Exit YTM (%)",ylabel="Realized annual return (%)")
axes[1].legend(fontsize=8)
fig.tight_layout();plt.show()
```

For this two-year horizon, a higher sale yield lowers the value of the remaining
three-year bond. Higher reinvestment rates increase accumulated coupons. These
are opposing effects with different magnitudes and timing.

## Predict, change, explain

Predict whether a 100 bp increase in the **exit** yield raises or lowers realized
return. Keep the reinvestment rate fixed at 3%. Move the HTML control, then explain
why that change is not an increase in the return already earned.

```{python}
#| label: returns-explorer
explorer=horizon_report(yields,.03)
display(demo_explorer(100*yields,{
    "Two-year HPR":explorer["HPR (%)"].to_numpy(),
```

## Validation checks

```{python}
#| label: returns-checks
assert np.isclose(bond_price(.05,10,.05),100)
assert np.isclose(base["Annual return (%)"].iloc[0],5.0625)
assert np.all(np.diff(scenarios["Sale / principal"])<0)
assert scenarios["HPR (%)"].iloc[-1] < 0
assert np.allclose(scenarios["Terminal wealth"]-purchase_price,
    scenarios["Coupon cash"]+scenarios["Reinvestment income"]+scenarios["Price change"])
at_maturity=horizon_report([.01,.10],.05,10)
assert np.allclose(at_maturity["Sale / principal"],100)
assert np.allclose(at_maturity["Annual return (%)"],5.0625)
display(Markdown("**Passed:** par pricing, return-component reconciliation, sale-price monotonicity, and the YTM reinvestment benchmark through maturity."))
```

At maturity the exit yield no longer matters: principal is fixed. The accumulated
coupon value still depends on reinvestment rates. Between coupon dates, use full
purchase and sale prices, including accrued interest, and actual payment dates.

## Mini Project

**Project brief.** Prepare a one-page return memo for a client buying $2 million
face of this bond and selling after two years. The client expects a 3% coupon
reinvestment rate and considers exit YTMs of 3%, 5%, and 10%.

1. Report the cash purchase cost, terminal sale proceeds, coupons, reinvestment
   income, dollar profit, two-year HPR, and effective annual return for each case.
2. Explain why the 6% coupon and 5% purchase YTM differ from realized return.
3. Repeat the unchanged-exit-yield case with zero coupon reinvestment income.
4. Recommend whether the bond suits a client who cannot tolerate a two-year loss.
   State the model's limitations and identify a closer maturity match.

```{=html}
<details class="demo-solution"><summary>Worked solution: client return memo</summary>
```

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
**Worked solution: client return memo**
:::

```{python}
#| label: returns-mini-project
position_face=2_000_000
scale=position_face/100
report=scenarios.copy()
for col in ["Sale / principal","Coupon cash","Reinvestment income","Price change","Terminal wealth"]:
    report[col]*=scale
report["Profit ($)"]=(scenarios["Terminal wealth"]-purchase_price)*scale
display(Markdown(f"Purchase cost is **${purchase_price*scale:,.2f}**. Coupons received are **$240,000** over two years."))
show_table(report[["Exit YTM (%)","Sale / principal","Coupon cash"]],2)
show_table(report[["Exit YTM (%)","Reinvestment income","Profit ($)"]],2)
show_table(report[["Exit YTM (%)","HPR (%)","Annual return (%)"]],4)
show_table(horizon_report(.05,0)[["Reinvest (%)","Terminal wealth","HPR (%)","Annual return (%)"]],5)
```

**Interpretation and decision.** The coupon rate determines contractual cash
payments; it does not measure profit relative to the premium purchase price.
The purchase YTM describes promised cash-flow discounting, while the horizon
return also depends on sale price and reinvestment. The 10% exit scenario shows
that coupon income need not prevent a loss. This five-year bond does not assure
a positive two-year return. A default-free zero-coupon claim maturing at the
client's horizon better matches a fixed nominal liability and eliminates coupon
reinvestment risk. Its purchase price still determines its return; inflation,
transaction costs, and selling before maturity remain relevant.

```{=html}
</details>
```
